solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stores holding over copper taps

indicators.note: the stores wrap round, or hold, the letters for over and copper

parts.note: stocks are stores of goods
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a PC (police constable) is a copper, slang for a policeman

explanation.surface: A warehouse keeping a stock of copper taps for plumbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like the metal of the taps, but it is a policeman, PC.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopcocks are valves controlling water flow in pipes, a kind of tap.

clue.text: Half-hearted drinker loves to tour Lima, a lovely place to go?

indicators.note: the two loves trail after the Lima letter
one of the two middle letters, half of its heart, is lost

parts.note: a supper is one who sups, a drinker
L is Lima in the NATO alphabet
love is zero in tennis, O, so two loves give OO

explanation.surface: A drinker touring Peru's capital finds a pleasant place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' is a euphemism for using the toilet; 'Lima' looks like Peru's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A superloo is a high-tech public toilet, a nice place to relieve oneself.

clue.text: Revealed what solicitor did, blowing cover

indicators.note: losing its covering first letter

parts.note: to tout is to solicit custom, so a solicitor touted

explanation.surface: A lawyer exposing a secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a lawyer; it is anyone soliciting trade.
explanation.definitionFit: To out someone is to expose a secret about them, so outed means exposed.

clue.text: Sweary navy, perhaps, drunk in the main

parts.note: navy blue is an example of a colour

indicators.note: mostly, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: full is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Drunken sailors swearing out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'navy' and 'the main' (the sea) build a picture of sailors; both serve other jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Colourful language is rude, full of swear words.

clue.text: Reported crook, well-known speed merchant?

indicators.note: said out, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: a cheater is a crook, a swindler

explanation.surface: News of a famous fast criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is famed as the fastest land animal, a famous sprinter of the savannah.

clue.text: Victory in series when number one over gets dismissal

indicators.note: is sent away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a succession is a series
I is the Roman numeral one
on means over, as on top of

explanation.surface: A cricket win in a series when the top batsman is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Success and victory both mean winning, achieving the desired result.

clue.text: 9 arranged flower

indicators.note: the letters of the answer to clue 9 are set out in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 9 across is petal

explanation.surface: A flower arranged from the answer to another clue, read as floral display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, something that flows: the River Plate in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords often call a river a flower because it flows; the Plate is the South American estuary river.

clue.text: Fruit from Jewish festival left by sons

indicators.note: abandoned by, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Pesach is the Hebrew name for Passover
S is short for son

explanation.surface: Fruit from a religious feast that the boys didn't eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The peach is a soft stone fruit.

clue.text: Runs berserk, stabbing a sick old creature

indicators.note: the runs and berserk letters pierce the others

parts.note: ill means sick
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
mad means berserk

explanation.surface: A violent madman stabbing an ailing pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured South American mammal, an animal.

clue.text: Make attractive, as outerwear and headgear do

definitions.meaning: both these words finish, end, in the letters E-A-R

explanation.surface: Clothes and hats making a person look appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make loved or liked.

clue.text: 6ac arranged flower — just a bit of one

definitions.text: flower — just a bit of one

indicators.note: the letters of the answer to 6 across are set out in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 6 across is plate

explanation.surface: Arranging a flower, but only one small piece of it.
explanation.walkthrough: This mirrors 6 across: here 'flower' is a real bloom, and the definition is a part of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is one of the coloured segments making up a bloom, just a bit of the whole.

clue.text: Cried out as other half once made demands

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, someone's other half in the past
claimed means demanded as a right

explanation.surface: Someone shouting as a former spouse once insisted on things.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to shout suddenly, so the past tense matches cried out.

clue.text: Fieldwork concerning question

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to doubt something is to question it

explanation.surface: Raising a query about some research done in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fieldwork' suggests research outdoors; it is a temporary military earthwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a temporary fortification built in the field by soldiers, which is military fieldwork.

clue.text: Prickly sort of letter penned by a dame

indicators.note: the letter is enclosed, as if penned in, by the dame's name

parts.note: Dame Edna Everage, the comic character played by Barry Humphries
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A spiky letter written by an elderly lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, is covered in spines, so it is a prickly kind of animal.

clue.text: Wonderful ET

definitions.meaning: the extra-terrestrial from the film comes from beyond our planet

explanation.surface: A short verdict on the Spielberg film.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both marvellous and, literally, from another planet like the alien.

clue.text: PM show including parodies on a regular basis

indicators.note: the teaching word goes around the picked letters

parts.note: to teach is to show someone how

indicators.note: every other letter of parodies is taken

explanation.surface: A TV show that keeps lampooning the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second letter of parodies gives AOIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the Prime Minister of Ireland.

clue.text: One's superior throughout marriage

parts.note: over, as in all over, throughout
a match is a marriage

explanation.surface: A spouse who is dominant for the whole of the marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An overmatch is an opponent better than oneself, a stronger rival.

clue.text: Pants, as footballers maybe around end of run

indicators.note: the kicking word goes round the final letter

parts.note: footballers are kickers, people who kick a ball

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one letter of run is used

explanation.surface: Football shorts worn at the end of a training run.
explanation.walkthrough: In British use 'pants' are underwear, so knickers fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are women's underpants, and pants in Britain means underwear.

clue.text: Parisian refusal put on commune eating aristo food, say

indicators.note: the French refusal is placed after the commune in the answer

parts.note: a collective is a commune of people sharing work

indicators.note: the refusal takes in the aristocratic letter

parts.note: non is French for no
U means upper class, aristocratic

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat refusing to eat a commune's food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'food' is a mass word naming many items together, as 'flock' or 'herd' does.
explanation.definitionFit: Food is offered as an example of a word grouping many things, a grammatical term for such words.

clue.text: Vain chap's cross, caught in valley

indicators.note: the cross and caught letters go inside the valley

parts.note: a coomb is a short valley or hollow
X is a cross
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A conceited man trapped and angry in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry; it is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a conceited dandy, a fop.

clue.text: To sum up, I go under about hiding answer

indicators.note: the turned-round word conceals the answer letter
the word for go under is turned round

parts.note: to drown is to go under water

explanation.surface: A defeated speaker summing up as they go under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns DROWN to NWORD, with A then put within.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means briefly, summing a matter up in one term.

clue.text: Sole college question on English

indicators.note: the question letters come on top of English, before it

parts.note: uni is short for university

explanation.surface: The only exam question at college about English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like the fish; it means one and only.
explanation.definitionFit: Unique means the only one of its kind.

clue.text: Robin's temporary accommodation in unassailable fort, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: best in the sense of unbeatable, beyond challenge
Fort Knox, the US bullion depository famed as impregnable

explanation.surface: A bird lodging in a fortress that cannot be attacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BEST KNOX gives NEST BOX.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden box put up for birds to nest in is temporary housing for a robin during breeding.

clue.text: Pipe from India received by brother

indicators.note: taken in by the brother word

parts.note: Brer is brother, as in Brer Rabbit
I is India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A pipe sent from India to a brother.
explanation.definitionFit: A brier is a tobacco pipe made from briar root.

clue.text: Annual account about chap in Los Angeles

indicators.note: the account letters go around the rest
the chap sits inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A yearly report on a man living in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Annual' looks like an adjective; it is a noun, a book published each year.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a reference book issued every year, so it is a yearly publication.

clue.text: Spies Poles burying chest

indicators.note: the poles enclose the chest

parts.note: N and S, the north and south poles
an ark is a chest, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Spies burying a chest in Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Narks are informers, police spies.

clue.text: Novel campanologist the Sunday after Easter

definitions.meaning: the bell-ringer hunchback of Notre Dame in Victor Hugo's novel
Low Sunday is named in Latin from its introit's opening words

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer at church on Low Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugo's hunchback was a foundling named after the Sunday when he was found, which also bears the name.

clue.text: Number 27 is wrong

indicators.note: the letters of the other clue's answer are put wrongly, in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 27 across is ether

explanation.surface: Someone declaring the figure in another puzzle answer incorrect.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is an integer, a counting figure.

clue.text: Number 26 is wrong

indicators.note: the letters of the other clue's answer are put wrongly, in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 26 across is three

explanation.surface: Someone declaring the figure in another puzzle answer incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Number' as 'something that numbs', not a figure as in 26.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early anaesthetic, something that makes a patient numb, hence a numb-er.

clue.text: Adherents of cleric, last out of church, first to enter coach

indicators.note: the cleric and following letters go inside the coach

parts.note: a bus is a coach
DD, Doctor of Divinity, a churchman's degree

indicators.note: only the final letter is taken from the word church

parts.note: 1st, written IST with I for one

explanation.surface: Followers of a priest, the last to leave church and first onto the coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddhists follow the teachings of the Buddha, so they are adherents of that faith.
